question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $f(x)=2 x^{2} + 2 x + 1$. Differentiate:

$$
f'(x)=4 x + 2
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope at the supplied abscissa:

$$
m_t=f'\left(-1\right)=4 \left(-1\right) + 2=-2
$$

The normal is perpendicular to the tangent, so

$$
m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}=-\frac{1}{\left(-2\right)}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

Use the point in point-slope form and rearrange:

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-\left(1\right)&=\frac{1}{2}\left(x-\left(-1\right)\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{2}+\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)+\left(1\right)\\
y&=\frac{x}{2} + \frac{3}{2}
\end{aligned}
$$

Thus $a=\frac{1}{2}$ and $b=\frac{3}{2}$.

question.:question/problem:
Find where the normal line to the curve $y=- x^{3} - 2$ at the point $(-2,6)$ intersects the $x$-axis.

The intersection is $(${{field-1}}$,$ {{field-2}}$)$. Give exact values.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Differentiate the polynomial.

$$
f'(x)=- 3 x^{2}.
$$

Evaluate the tangent slope and take its negative reciprocal to find the normal slope.

$$
\begin{aligned}
m_t=f'(-2)&=- 3 (-2)^{2}=-12, \\m_n=-\frac{1}{m_t}&=-\frac{1}{(-12)}=\frac{1}{12}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Use point-slope form through $(-2,6)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
y-(6)&=\frac{1}{12}(x-(-2)), \\y&=\frac{x}{12} + \frac{37}{6}.
\end{aligned}
$$

At the $x$-axis, $y=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
0&=\frac{1}{12}x+\left(\frac{37}{6}\right), \\x&=-74.
\end{aligned}
$$

The intersection is $(-74,0)$.
